newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel cargo prices firmer after active trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel cargo prices firmer after active trade.

text.p: NWE diesel cargo prices were slightly firmer after a flurry of trade on Tuesday, but heating oil markets were unchanged to slightly softer with supplies good and buyers relaxed, traders said.
Around six diesel cargoes were traded on Tuesday at premiums between July IPE +$5.50 and +$6.50 per tonne depending on date and delivery point, four into French ports and two into ARA.
Additionally an Algerian cargo was sold prompt into Antwerp at July +$6.75 a tonne.

Early July Diesel premiums were assessed around July IPE +$6/+$7 a tonne based on Tuesday's activity but early trade was thin. 0.2 sulphur premiums talked in a slightly wider range with the IPE screen contango of $2 keeping buyers and sellers apart.

Prompt 0.2 sulphur deliveries valued around July screen evens with good prompt supplies leaving buyers looking for discounts, while July 1-15 cargo bids were screen evens at best, sellers, eyeing the futures contango looked for July IPE +$1 per tonne.

The ARA barge market for heating oil talked on a two-tier basis with tighter refinery supplies taking a small premium to storage material. Prompt lifting storage barges were trade from July IPE -50 cents up to screen evens with a Rotterdam refinery barge taking July IPE +25 cents.
Antwerp and Flushing lifting diesel barges were assessed around July IPE +$4/+$5 with Rotterdam loadings asking +$6 a tonne.
